modelNotes.districtUnit: A voter record has an implicit integer ID; each segment stores a lossless contiguous range sharing state, district, and affiliation. Expanding ranges gives exactly 1,550,000 records.
modelNotes.population: State sample weights use EAVS active registration counts from 2024. Within states, unchanged congressional districts use 2020-2024 ACS CVAP. Alabama, California, Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, and Utah use 2026 district vote totals to apportion their ACS state CVAP over the redrawn 2026 districts.
modelNotes.affiliation: Reported registration shares are based on Ballotpedia August 2026 state registration tables. States without party registration use a modeled split calibrated to the 2024 state presidential margin and the national party-affiliation mix. District Democratic/Republican shares are adjusted using district lean while preserving each state total.
modelNotes.thirdParty: Reported “other parties” are apportioned between Green, Libertarian, and other minor parties using national 2026 registered minor-party shares; this split is an estimate.

factions.name: The Liberal Establishment
factions.flavor: The traditional backbone of the Democratic Party—elected officials, party apparatus loyalists, and suburban pragmatists who favor steady governance, institutional guardrails, and incremental reform.

factions.name: Black Voters
factions.flavor: The African American Voting Block - have been a core faction of the democratic party since the civil rights movement

factions.name: The Capital L Left
factions.flavor: Extreme on Rhetoric, Extreme on Policy - these are the progressives that are keeping fox news in business

factions.name: Neo-Liberals
factions.flavor: Pro-globalization, free-trade technocrats and educated professionals who combine socially progressive values with market-oriented economic policies and fiscal prudence.

factions.name: Abundance
factions.flavor: Pro-building, supply-side liberals and state-capacity reformers focused on abundant housing, rapid clean-energy permitting, high-speed transit, and modernizing government to deliver tangible growth.

factions.name: Bernie Bros
factions.flavor: These are voters who became engaged in politics during Bernie Sanders 2016 campaign. They’re milder on social views and rhetoric, but very left leaning on economic issues. It also has a strong populist current.

factions.name: Faith Based Liberals
factions.flavor: Mainline Protestant, Catholic, and interfaith social-gospel voters who view progressive politics as a moral duty to care for the poor, marginalized, and vulnerable.

factions.name: Blue Dog Democrats
factions.flavor: Fiscally conservative and culturally moderate Democrats who represent rural, small-town, and border districts, emphasizing bipartisan compromise and deficit reduction.

factions.name: Traditional Latin Voters
factions.flavor: Multi-generational Hispanic and Latino families in urban centers and agricultural belts who blend socially moderate family values with support for public education and healthcare access.

factions.name: Faith & Flag Conservatives
factions.flavor: Evangelical and devout traditionalist Christians who prioritize social conservatism, judicial originalism, and the defense of religious institutions in public life.

factions.name: Nationalist Populists (MAGA)
factions.flavor: America-First working-class nationalists energized by Donald Trump, emphasizing strict border enforcement, protectionist trade policies, and cultural populism.

factions.name: Liberty & Western Mavericks
factions.flavor: Rugged individualists, ranchers, and Second Amendment absolutists across the Mountain West who demand federal land divestment and radical regulatory relief.

factions.name: Blood and Soil Nationalists
factions.flavor: Hardline nativist reactionaries who demand an end to legal immigration, aggressive deportation operations, and the cultural reassertion of European heritage.

factions.name: Frontier & Suburban Moderates
factions.flavor: College-educated suburbanites and Sunbelt professionals who favor pro-business tax policy and public safety while rejecting conspiratorial rhetoric and cultural extremism.

factions.name: Neo-Cons
factions.flavor: Hawkish foreign policy institutionalists and defense-sector advocates who champion global American hegemony, democratic interventionism, and deterrence against authoritarian rivals.

factions.name: Paleocons
factions.flavor: Old-Right isolationists who combine deep cultural traditionalism with fierce opposition to foreign wars, global trade pacts, and centralized federal power.

factions.name: Mormons
factions.flavor: Latter-day Saint voters across the Intermountain West who pair devout family values and fiscal conservatism with institutional decency, civic trust, and welcoming refugee attitudes.

factions.name: Traditional Farmers
factions.flavor: Generational agricultural producers and rural smallholders who depend on farm bill protections, biofuel mandates, and water rights while maintaining traditional cultural leanings.

factions.name: Market & Country-Club Conservatives
factions.flavor: Wealthy corporate executives, financiers, and donors who focus primarily on supply-side tax cuts, capital gains relief, and minimal government intervention in capital markets.

factions.name: Cubans
factions.flavor: South Florida Cuban-American voting bloc with deep anti-communist convictions, fiercely loyal to hardline foreign policy against Latin American dictatorships and supportive of free-market policies.

factions.name: True Centrists
factions.flavor: The perfect ideological center of the American electorate, evenly divided and skeptical of ideological purity from both parties, deciding general election outcomes.

factions.name: Hard Hats
factions.flavor: Union Voters and Construction workers used to be reliably democratic - but the Trump Coalition swallowed them up

factions.name: Podcast Bros
factions.flavor: These low information voters get most of their news from podcasts - and that’s how they decide on who they vote for, too

factions.name: Country Club Centrists
factions.flavor: These voters used to be dyed in the wool republicans - but Trump changed everything

factions.name: Technocrats
factions.flavor: These voters believe in the power of technology. They hold progressive social views (civil rights, free speech) but despise regulatory barriers, compute controls, and wealth taxes.

factions.name: Grillers
factions.flavor: These voters don’t follow politics closely - they just want to be left alone and grill. But when food, gas, and energy prices spike, they deliver brutal verdicts to the governing party.

factions.name: Religious Moderates
factions.flavor: Churchgoers, Catholics, and interfaith believers who resist hard-right Christian nationalism but expect politicians to respect personal faith, family values, and basic community compassion.

factions.name: Working Class Latinos
factions.flavor: Blue-collar Hispanic voters in Nevada, Arizona, Texas, and the Rust Belt who prioritize steady jobs, law and order, and small-business opportunity, swinging fluidly between both major parties.

factions.name: Girlypops
factions.flavor: Young, pop-culture-fluent women who care deeply about reproductive autonomy, social equality, and campus climate, but distrust career politicians and rigid ideological labels.

factions.name: True Libertarians
factions.flavor: True libertarians are hard to come by - but these voters believe in true small government, not just on liberal issues

factions.name: Ancaps
factions.flavor: These voters don’t think the government should exist.

factions.name: Eco-Socialist Vanguard
factions.flavor: The Eco-Socialist Vanguard warns of the coming eco-apoclypse

factions.name: YIMBYs
factions.flavor: These leftie voters left the democrats over housing issues - now they’re in an uncomfortable alliance with the greens

factions.name: Christian Dominionists & Theocrats
factions.flavor: Radical religious reconstructionists who believe American civil law should be completely replaced with biblical law and Christian governance.

factions.name: Socialists
factions.flavor: These voters are socialists, who idealize Karl Marx.

factions.name: Communists
factions.flavor: These are communists, who want total state control over the economy.

factions.name: Groypers
factions.flavor: Online alt-right provocateurs and youth reactionaries who use irony, memes, and internet culture to push far-right ethno-nationalist talking points into mainstream discourse.

factions.name: The Klan & Neo-Nazis
factions.flavor: These voters support the Klu Klux Klan and Neo-Nazis. They turn out 0%.
